goal: Recover missing per-kernel module installation from source registration and build records.
context: Prerequisites: saved kernel builds, per-release module trees and a preserved boot fallback.

concepts.title: One source, several kernel instances
concepts.text: DKMS helps maintain extra kernel modules from source when kernels change. A module is a separately loadable piece of kernel code. This lesson supplies build-ready training sources and two kernels; nothing is downloaded or compiled on your computer.

concepts.title: Read added, built and installed
concepts.text: Added means a source version is registered. Built means an instance has been prepared for a particular kernel and architecture. Installed means its object has been placed in that kernel’s module tree. Installed does not mean loaded or that a device works. A label such as survey-net/0.8 gives the module package name followed by its version. The equivalent -m option supplies the package name and -v supplies its version.

concepts.title: Choose the kernel deliberately
concepts.text: In the console, type a supported command and select Run. dkms status inspects the registry. -k names one supplied kernel; without it, build/install/uninstall use the displayed running kernel. A newly prepared kernel is not automatically the running one.

concepts.title: Connect preparation to installation
concepts.text: dkms build can register a missing supplied source. dkms install can register and build as needed. You may use separate add, build and install steps, or install directly. A built result still needs installation before the target requirement is met.

worked.label: Supplied example
worked.explanation: These example facts differ from the independent assignment. Both use supplied training inputs.

worked.label: Inspect
worked.explanation: Expected: the running kernel already has survey-net/0.8 installed. Actual output appears below the console only after Run.

worked.label: Prepare
worked.explanation: Expected: built for the maintenance kernel. This has not installed it.

worked.label: Place
worked.explanation: Expected: installed for the maintenance kernel. The module/version form is equivalent. Direct install can also add/build when needed.

practice.title: Inspect the supplied instances
practice.action: Enter dkms status in the console and select Run. Find the running and maintenance kernels in Actual console results.
practice.observe: Each line identifies the module/version, kernel and architecture. An added source alone has no per-kernel instance.

practice.title: Prepare and target the change
practice.action: Run dkms build survey-net/0.8 -k 6.1.121. Read its result, then run dkms install survey-net/0.8 -k 6.1.121.
practice.observe: Built and installed are different results. Omitting -k would select the supplied running kernel instead of the maintenance target.

practice.title: Verify, break and retry
practice.action: Run dkms status -k 6.1.121, then select Check configuration. Uninstall survey-net/0.8 only for 6.1.121 and check again; reinstall it to repair the target.
practice.observe: A state-changing operation clears the last check. The failed row explains which version/kernel is missing; read-only status does not break a correct configuration.

requirements: Preserve every supplied module record for running fallback kernel 6.6.60. No module-loading test is required or simulated.

goal: Inspect two module versions, prepare a replacement and preserve another kernel’s known state.
context: Prerequisites: saved kernel builds, per-release module trees and a preserved boot fallback. Complete the per-kernel DKMS recovery lesson first.

concepts.text: DKMS helps maintain extra kernel modules from source when kernels change. A module is a separately loadable piece of kernel code. This lesson supplies build-ready training sources and two kernels; nothing is downloaded or compiled on your computer.

concepts.title: Prepare a targeted version handover
concepts.text: Build the replacement for the maintenance kernel first. In this subset, explicitly uninstall the older target instance, then install the replacement. Uninstall leaves its built record available. Automatic replacement, version sanity checks and original-module backups are outside the simulator, so a conflicting direct installation is honestly refused.

worked.explanation: These example facts differ from the independent assignment. Both use supplied training inputs.

worked.label: Inspect
worked.explanation: Expected: the running kernel already has survey-net/0.8 installed. Actual output appears below the console only after Run.

worked.label: Prepare replacement
worked.explanation: Expected: a built instance for the maintenance kernel; the old installed version still remains there.

worked.label: Targeted handover
worked.value:
dkms uninstall survey-net/0.8 -k 6.1.121
dkms install survey-net/0.9 -k 6.1.121
worked.explanation: Run each command separately. Expected: old target instance built, new target installed, running kernel still on 0.8.

practice.action: Enter dkms status in the console and select Run. Find the running and maintenance kernels in Actual console results.
practice.observe: Each line identifies the module/version, kernel and architecture. An added source alone has no per-kernel instance.

practice.title: Prepare and target the change
practice.action:
Run each command separately with Run:
dkms build survey-net/0.9 -k 6.1.121
dkms uninstall survey-net/0.8 -k 6.1.121
dkms install survey-net/0.9 -k 6.1.121
practice.observe: The replacement is built before installation; uninstall leaves the previous version built. The running kernel’s instance stays unchanged.

practice.action: Run dkms status -k 6.1.121, then select Check configuration. Uninstall survey-net/0.9 only for 6.1.121 and check again; reinstall it to repair the target.
